decisions.reason: As a design-led line close to existing decorative fabrics, it likely faced direct comparison with internal alternatives and, after several seasons, a merely uncertain payoff would fall below aspiration levels and be pruned to free warehouse and sampling capacity.

This transparent burnout fabric is near the firm’s core offer but also overlaps with other decorative launches, so boundedly rational management would be inclined to drop it if it did not clearly outperform comparable lines by 2022.

Because it is a single burnout decorative fabric rather than a broader line, it offers less scope for variation and learning, making it more likely to be judged below aspiration and removed in favor of stronger established products or new development.

A velour-like upholstery fabric fits the firm’s established upholstery business well, and the firm’s service, stocking, and reorder capabilities give enough slack to keep a core-adjacent product unless results are clearly disappointing.

The flame-retardant inbetween fabric extends the offer in a functionally differentiated way that can support dependable supply to trade customers, so management would likely keep it while its performance remains plausibly at or near aspiration.

The polyester lining fabric is related to the existing offer but appears more peripheral to the firm’s design-led decorative and upholstery strengths, so if its sales were only moderate management would likely reallocate resources away from it.
